name: Ketamine

binding.assay_buffer_notes: Used as the reference comparator in Roth 2013 (MK-801 Ki ≈ 5.7 nM in same assay)
binding.notes: Racemic ketamine; widely cited canonical value
S-ketamine ~4× higher affinity than R-ketamine

binding.tissue_or_cell: recombinant human GluN1/GluN2A NMDA receptor (Xenopus oocytes)
binding.notes: Zhang et al. 2021 Nature (PMID 34321660). S-ketamine IC50 0.60 µM at the human NMDA receptor; ~4× more potent than R-ketamine, matching Oye 1992 human-brain data.

binding.tissue_or_cell: recombinant human GluN1/GluN2A NMDA receptor (Xenopus oocytes)
binding.notes: Zhang et al. 2021 Nature (PMID 34321660). R-ketamine IC50 2.39 µM at the human NMDA receptor.
R-ketamine Ki ≈ 27,000 nM, S-ketamine Ki ≈ 131,000 nM at σ1; substantial enantioselectivity
Very weak; clinical relevance unclear

binding.tissue_or_cell: recombinant mu-opioid receptor expressed in CHO cells (CHO-mu)
binding.notes: Hirota et al. 1997; functional agonism debated. Williams 2018 naltrexone trial showed naltrexone blocks ketamine antidepressant effect but Yoon 2019 reanalysis questioned methodology

binding.tissue_or_cell: recombinant kappa-opioid receptor expressed in CHO cells (CHO-kappa)

functional.cell_system: HEK293 expressing HCN1; cortical pyramidal neurons
functional.notes: EC50 ~8-16 μM for racemate; S-ketamine ~2× more potent (EC50 ~7 μM). Within clinically anesthetic free plasma range (5-10 μM). Chen et al. 2009 — HCN1 knockout abolishes ketamine hypnosis

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Acute: blocks open NMDA channel (use-dependent, voltage-sensitive). Disinhibits cortical pyramidal cells via preferential blockade of GABAergic interneuron NMDARs → glutamate surge → AMPA activation → BDNF/TrkB → mTORC1 → synaptogenesis (Duman/Aghajanian model). HCN1 inhibition contributes to hypnosis. The major active metabolite (2R,6R)-HNK potentiates AMPA via α7 nAChR-dependent presynaptic mechanism (Marcantoni 2024, doi:10.1038/s41398-024-02744-y).

neuroimaging.finding: Acute ketamine increases prefrontal/ACC BOLD signal and decreases default-mode network connectivity in humans; matches subjective dissociation
Acute ketamine increases gamma power (30-80 Hz), decreases alpha power; biomarker of dissociation and rapid antidepressant response
[11C]-(+)-PHNO displacement studies show ketamine increases striatal dopamine release ~20% at subanesthetic doses (consistent with ~3% D2/D3 occupancy by displaced DA)

routes.notes: Clements & Nimmo 1981. Terminal t½ ~2.5 h (range 2-4 h)
Yanagihara et al. report 45% absolute bioavailability; some studies give 25-50% range
Grant et al. 1981; oral bioavailability 17-20% due to extensive first-pass; norketamine/ketamine ratio ~6.4 in plasma with oral route

concentration_effect.notes: Plasma ketamine ~640-1000 ng/mL produces unconsciousness; recovery at <500 ng/mL
Subanesthetic plasma ~100-200 ng/mL during 0.5 mg/kg IV infusion produces analgesia and antidepressant response

metabolism.notes: Yanagihara 2002, Hijazi 2002. CYP2B6 demethylates S- and R-ketamine equipotently
CYP3A4 demethylates S-ketamine faster than R-ketamine; primary in human liver microsomes per some reports
HNK does NOT block NMDA at antidepressant-relevant doses (Zanos 2016, Suzuki 2017 doi:10.1073/pnas.1816071116); acts via α7 nAChR and AMPA potentiation

drug_interactions_pk.clinical_effect: Oral ketamine AUC increased ~2.6× by clarithromycin (strong CYP3A4 inhibitor)
Inhibits norketamine formation; increases ketamine AUC

pharmacogenetics.phenotype_effects: CYP2B6 516 G>T carriers showed roughly 2.4-fold higher oral esketamine plasma levels than non-carriers (median 5.1 vs 2.1 ug/L, p=0.032) in a small treatment-resistant-depression sample (n=18); no significant effect was seen on metabolite levels, or for CYP3A4*22 or CYP3A5*3.

tolerance_and_dependence.receptor_downregulation_half_time: Rapid tachyphylaxis with repeated dosing (hours to days); use-dependence of NMDA blockade reduces with sustained channel blockade
cross_tolerance: DXM (partial, via different NMDA site kinetics)
tolerance_and_dependence.withdrawal_syndrome: Mild compared to opioids/benzos. Onset 24-72h after cessation in heavy users: craving, dysphoria, anhedonia, fatigue, GI distress. Lasts 1-2 weeks. Urinary tract symptoms (ketamine cystitis) may persist months.

off_targets.clinical_consequence: Contributes to hypnotic action; HCN1 KO mice resistant to ketamine anesthesia
Minor at clinical concentrations; indirect sympathomimetic effects dominate cardiovascular profile
Inhibition at supratherapeutic doses; not clinically dominant
Ulcerative cystitis in chronic high-dose users (>1 g/day); norketamine implicated as direct urothelial toxin

demographic_differences.sex: Women have slightly lower CL/F and higher peak exposure on weight-normalized basis
demographic_differences.age: Pediatric CL/kg higher than adult; elderly show decreased CL
demographic_differences.weight: Standard weight-based dosing; obese patients may need lean-body-weight calculation
demographic_differences.renal_or_hepatic: Hepatic impairment reduces CL significantly; renal impairment minor effect on parent but HNK glucuronides accumulate

data_gaps_remaining: definitive μ-opioid functional agonism vs allosteric modulation; mechanism of urothelial toxicity
notes: Reference compound for the entire class. Zhang 2021 Nature (doi:10.1038/s41586-021-03769-9) revealed S-ketamine binds NMDA channel central vestibule with two distinct sub-poses; key residues GluN2A-L642 and GluN1-N616. R-ketamine has longer-lasting/stronger antidepressant effect in rodents despite lower NMDA affinity (Hashimoto group).

name: Esketamine

binding.notes: Ebert 1997; ~4× higher affinity than R-ketamine. Some sources report 560 nM.

binding.tissue_or_cell: recombinant mu-opioid receptor expressed in CHO cells (CHO-mu)
binding.notes: Hirota 1997

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Same as racemic ketamine but ~2× more potent. FDA approval (Spravato 2019) for TRD relies on NMDA-mediated disinhibition + downstream synaptogenesis.

neuroimaging.finding: Spravato 84 mg intranasal increases ACC and PFC activation, decreases DMN connectivity in TRD patients

routes.notes: Janssen Spravato label; Tmax 20-40 min, terminal t½ ~7-12 h. Plasma can be measured within 7 min.

metabolism.notes: CYP3A4 demethylates S-ketamine faster than R-ketamine

pharmacogenetics.phenotype_effects: CYP2B6 PMs show higher esketamine exposure; clinical dose adjustment not specified by Spravato label

tolerance_and_dependence.receptor_downregulation_half_time: Tachyphylaxis with frequent dosing; Spravato dosing is twice-weekly induction then weekly/biweekly
tolerance_and_dependence.withdrawal_syndrome: Similar to ketamine; not formally characterized for esketamine alone

demographic_differences.age: Elderly (≥65): clearance reduced; dose adjustment per label
demographic_differences.renal_or_hepatic: Moderate hepatic impairment: AUC ↑ ~58%; severe hepatic impairment not studied

notes: FDA-approved 2019 as Spravato (intranasal) for treatment-resistant depression and 2020 for major depressive disorder with acute suicidal ideation. Same PK/PD parameters apply to S-Ketamine record.

name: S-Ketamine

binding.notes: Same compound as Esketamine record; entry retained because input list contains both names.

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: See Esketamine record.

notes: Chemically identical to Esketamine. Input list has both names — Piru likely benefits from a dedup pass.

name: Arketamine

binding.notes: Ebert 1997. ~4-5× lower affinity than S-ketamine.
5× higher σ1 affinity than S-ketamine; Hashimoto hypothesizes σ1 agonism mediates arketamine's longer antidepressant effect.

binding.tissue_or_cell: recombinant mu-opioid receptor expressed in CHO cells (CHO-mu)

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Hashimoto group has consistently shown R-ketamine produces longer-lasting (>1 week) antidepressant-like effects in rodents than S-ketamine despite lower NMDA affinity. Mechanism proposed: σ1 agonism + sustained BDNF-TrkB-mTOR signalling + ERK pathway in mPFC. Phase 2a (Perception Neuroscience PCN-101) failed primary endpoint May 2023 but showed signal at 60 mg without dissociation.

neuroimaging.finding: (R)-ketamine produces distinctly different theta power changes vs (S)-ketamine — possibly tied to differential σ1 engagement

routes.notes: Perception Neuroscience PCN-101 IV-to-SC bridging study; SC well-tolerated

metabolism.notes: CYP2B6 demethylates both enantiomers similarly; CYP3A4 prefers S-ketamine

pharmacogenetics.phenotype_effects: CYP2B6 PMs likely show larger exposure increases for arketamine than esketamine because CYP3A4 contribution is smaller

tolerance_and_dependence.withdrawal_syndrome: Lower dissociation than esketamine; abuse potential likely lower

notes: Hashimoto group has driven most of the preclinical arketamine literature (2014-present). Major theoretical interest because lower NMDA blockade + longer antidepressant effect challenges the simple 'NMDA antagonism = antidepressant' model.

name: Norketamine

binding.notes: Ebert 1997. S-norketamine Ki ~1700 nM; R-norketamine Ki ~13,000 nM. About 3× less potent than parent ketamine at NMDA. After oral ketamine, norketamine plasma >> ketamine plasma (ratio ~6:1) — major contributor to oral PD.

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Same use-dependent NMDA channel block as parent. Higher norketamine/ketamine ratio with oral route makes norketamine a major active species in oral ketamine PD.

routes.notes: Norketamine forms via first-pass; plasma half-life ~5-6 h, longer than parent ketamine

off_targets.clinical_consequence: Proposed primary mediator of ketamine cystitis in chronic users

notes: Tag 'no-human-data' is wrong — norketamine is detected in every human ketamine PK study; it's an active metabolite, not a research chemical.

name: Hydroxynorketamine

binding.notes: Suzuki 2017: (2R,6R)-HNK does NOT block NMDA at antidepressant-relevant concentrations (≤10 μM). Earlier Moaddel 2013 claim of NMDA antagonism not replicated. HNK binds closed/desensitized NMDA receptors at much higher concentrations (Lumsden 2019)

functional.notes: Marcantoni 2024: HNK (not ketamine) acts via α7-nAChR. Selective α7 antagonist or Chrna7 KO abolishes HNK-induced synaptic and nuclear regulations.
Zanos 2016: (2R,6R)-HNK potentiates AMPA via presynaptic mechanism. AMPA blockade by NBQX abolishes antidepressant effect.

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Proposed mechanism (Zanos/Gould): presynaptic α7-nAChR activation → glutamate release → AMPA potentiation → BDNF → TrkB → mTOR → synaptogenesis WITHOUT NMDA blockade or dissociation. This decoupling drove HNK as a non-dissociative antidepressant candidate (Phase 1 NIH 2023).

routes.notes: NIH Phase 1 single ascending dose study (Zarate group); preliminary data shows oral bioavailability adequate for therapeutic exposure

tolerance_and_dependence.withdrawal_syndrome: Predicted minimal (no NMDA blockade, no dissociation)

notes: Major mechanism controversy. Zarate/Gould (NIH) push α7-nAChR + AMPA mechanism (Zanos 2016 Nature, Marcantoni 2024 Transl Psychiatry). Moaddel 2013 originally claimed NMDA antagonism but Suzuki 2017 PNAS showed no NMDA block at antidepressant-relevant doses. Different from parent ketamine — should NOT be tagged NMDA-antagonist.

name: Dehydronorketamine

binding.notes: Essentially inactive at NMDA

functional.notes: Citation removed: this value was attributed to doi:10.1124/jpet.112.198887, which is cardiac late-sodium-current inhibitors. Verified against PubMed/Crossref in the 2026-08-01 topicality audit. The number is retained but is now unsourced — treat as unverified. DHNK is a negative allosteric modulator of α7-nAChR at low μM; opposite direction to HNK

notes: Major terminal metabolite of ketamine; long half-life (~12 h). Plasma DHNK is a marker of chronic ketamine exposure.

name: PCP

binding.notes: Roth 2013. Range across literature 59-250 nM; PCP is reference parent compound
Ki >10,000 nM in Roth 2013
Ki >10,000 nM in direct binding; functional DA-releasing effects may involve allosteric sites

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Strong NMDA channel block + indirect dopaminergic effects via σ-receptor-mediated DA release modulation in NAc (Nishikawa 1999, doi:10.1016/S0014-2999(99)00769-4).

neuroimaging.modality: phMRI (relative cerebral blood volume), anesthetized rat
neuroimaging.finding: PCP (0.5 mg/kg i.v.) produces robust, sustained rCBV increases across cortico-limbo-thalamic regions, the circuit signature used as a model of NMDAR-hypofunction schizophrenia; clozapine abolishes the thalamic component while raclopride has no effect

routes.notes: Cook 1982; t½ 1-3 days, mean ~21 h. Vd highly variable due to lipophilicity.

metabolism.metabolite_name: PCHP, c-PPC and t-PPC (piperidine-ring hydroxylation products)
p-hydroxy-PCP (4-hydroxy-PCP), which decomposes spontaneously to an electrophilic quinone methide

tolerance_and_dependence.receptor_downregulation_half_time: Tolerance develops to subjective effects within days of repeated use
tolerance_and_dependence.withdrawal_syndrome: Heavy chronic users: anxiety, depression, craving, weight loss, sleep disturbance; psychotic symptoms may persist weeks

demographic_differences.renal_or_hepatic: Highly lipophilic → enterohepatic recycling; gastric lavage useful in overdose

notes: Originally Parke-Davis Sernyl (1956); withdrawn from human use 1965 due to emergence delirium. Schedule II in US. Roth 2013 found PCP highly selective NMDA+σ2 with weak DAT/σ1. Two binding poses at PCP site (Zhang 2021 Nature, doi:10.1038/s41586-021-03769-9) explain SAR discrepancies across the class.

name: 3-MeO-PCP

binding.notes: Roth 2013. Among the most potent NMDA antagonists in the arylcyclohexylamine class — ~3× more potent than PCP, ~30× more than ketamine.
Some sources cite 436 nM. The high σ1 affinity (42 nM if accurate) at clinically achievable concentrations may explain the distinctive agitation/psychosis profile.

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Most NMDA-potent compound in the class. Combination of high-affinity NMDA blockade + σ1 agonism + SERT inhibition may explain unique agitation/mania/psychosis profile distinct from ketamine, MXE.

routes.notes: Estimated t½ 10-11 h from case reports; no controlled PK studies in humans

concentration_effect.notes: Fatal range 50-3,525 ng/mL femoral blood (Bakota 2016, Chatterton 2017, Allard 2021)

metabolism.notes: Major metabolite is the 3-hydroxy demethylation product (3-OH-PCP), itself an NMDA antagonist and μ-opioid agonist

tolerance_and_dependence.receptor_downregulation_half_time: Rapid tolerance; users often escalate to maintain effects
tolerance_and_dependence.withdrawal_syndrome: Psychological dependence; agitation/psychosis on cessation in heavy users
tolerance_and_dependence.notes: Citation removed: this value was attributed to doi:10.1016/j.forsciint.2017.02.022, which is GHB cut-offs in biological samples. Verified against PubMed/Crossref in the 2026-08-01 topicality audit. The number is retained but is now unsourced — treat as unverified.

notes: Distinct clinical profile from MXE and ketamine — much higher agitation/mania/psychosis risk plus narrow therapeutic window. Multiple fatalities (Chatterton 2017 reported 7 deaths in Sweden 2014-2016). The combination of very high NMDA affinity, σ1 agonism, and SERT inhibition is essentially unique in the class.

name: 4-meo-pcp

binding.notes: Roth 2013. Lower NMDA affinity than 3-MeO isomer (20 nM) and lower than PCP (59 nM) — 4-position substitution disfavored at PCP site. PsychonautWiki cites 20 nM but Roth's reported value is 404 nM.
Notable σ2 activity

notes: Para-methoxy substitution → reduced NMDA affinity vs meta-methoxy (3-MeO-PCP); ~20× less potent at NMDA than 3-MeO isomer per Roth 2013 — opposite of what's often claimed in casual references. Often considered the 'gentlest' of the methoxy-PCP series.

name: Methoxetamine

binding.notes: Roth 2013 reported 259 ± 76 nM (some texts cite 337). ~3× higher NMDA affinity than ketamine.
S-(+)-MXE Ki 320 nM, R-(-)-MXE Ki 510 nM. Confirmed functional SERT inhibitor (Hondebrink 2017).
Ki >10,000 nM — surprisingly weak vs 3-MeO-PCP (42 nM)

functional.notes: Marti et al. 2021: MXE behavioral effects (motor facilitation, visual sensory inhibition, PPI disruption) attenuated by the 5-HT2 antagonists ketanserin and MDL 100907; in vivo microdialysis showed MXE alters 5-HT in medial prefrontal cortex and nucleus accumbens

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: NMDA blockade dominant; SERT inhibition contributes serotonergic component that may underlie the longer-duration and 'antidepressant-like' subjective profile vs ketamine.

off_targets.clinical_consequence: Marketed as 'bladder friendly' but unsubstantiated: 3 months of dosing in mice produced bladder inflammation and fibrosis plus tubular and glomerular renal damage, similar to comparable chronic-ketamine models.

notes: Most-studied of the post-2010 RC dissociatives. Combination of high-affinity NMDA blockade (Ki 259 nM) + SERT inhibition (Ki 481 nM) is the canonical 2'-oxo + 3-methoxy + N-ethyl pharmacophore. Designed by Lee 2010 (UK patent) as a putative analgesic.

name: DMXE

binding.notes: Bonaventura 2022 / Wallach group; IC50 ~0.68 μM. Less potent than MXE despite structural similarity.

notes: Methyl analogue of MXE (3-methyl in place of 3-methoxy). Sold post-2020 as MXE replacement. The 3-methyl substituent loses H-bonding capacity vs methoxy → expected reduction in NMDA affinity, consistent with IC50 679 nM.

name: Deoxymethoxetamine

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Same compound as DMXE record.

notes: Identical to DMXE; input list has both names — Piru should dedup.

name: Deschloroketamine

binding.notes: Štefková-Mazochová 2022. Comparable to ketamine; S-DCK ~3× more potent than R-DCK in inhibition of NMDA currents.

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Behaves as ketamine pharmacologically. Longer duration than ketamine likely due to slower phase-I metabolism (the 2-chlorine in ketamine accelerates CYP-mediated oxidation).

routes.notes: User-reported t½ longer than ketamine (~4-6 h vs 2-3 h); no controlled studies

tolerance_and_dependence.withdrawal_syndrome: Heavy users report craving, anxiety, dysphoria

notes: Removal of 2-chloro from ketamine — gives slower CYP metabolism and longer subjective duration. Štefková-Mazochová 2022 is the only published rigorous PK/PD study (rats).

name: 2-Fluorodeschloroketamine

binding.notes: Citation removed: this value was attributed to doi:10.1016/j.forsciint.2021.110815, which is trace elements in lung for seawater-drowning diagnosis. Verified against PubMed/Crossref in the 2026-08-01 topicality audit. The number is retained but is now unsourced — treat as unverified. No formal Ki measurement published as of 2024. Assumed similar to ketamine (Ki ~600 nM) based on F-for-Cl bioisostere logic.

routes.notes: Analytically confirmed in fatal and non-fatal cases (blood 457-5885 ug/L; hair up to ~80 ng/mg), with nor-2-FDCK and dihydro metabolites; insufflation is the predominant reported route, but no published route-specific dose-response or PK data exist.

notes: F-for-Cl bioisostere of ketamine. Multiple fatalities documented (Theofel 2024 doi:10.1093/jat/bkae003, Pelletier 2024 doi:10.1016/j.forsciint.2024). WHO ECDD critical review 2023 recommended scheduling.

name: 3-MeO-PCE

binding.notes: Roth 2013. ~3× lower NMDA potency than 3-MeO-PCP (20 nM); piperidine → N-ethyl loss of one ring lowers affinity.
Approximate; Roth reports 'appreciable σ1 affinity'

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Similar to 3-MeO-PCP profile but with N-ethyl on a cyclohexylamine scaffold (vs piperidine). Reported as more 'stimulating' than MXE.

routes.notes: Citation removed: this value was attributed to doi:10.1016/j.forsciint.2021.110815, which is trace elements in lung for seawater-drowning diagnosis. Verified against PubMed/Crossref in the 2026-08-01 topicality audit. The number is retained but is now unsourced — treat as unverified. Implicated in fatalities along with 2F-DCK

tolerance_and_dependence.withdrawal_syndrome: Reports of mania, agitation similar to 3-MeO-PCP

notes: Non-keto analogue of MXE; shares 3-methoxy substitution but lacks the 2'-oxo group. Has the same agitation/psychosis liability as 3-MeO-PCP per case reports.

name: Methoxmetamine
notes: N-methyl analogue of MXE (N-methyl instead of N-ethyl). Predicted similar NMDA affinity (200-400 nM) and SERT activity but no published binding data.

name: O-PCE

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Deschloro-N-ethyl analogue of ketamine. Predicted similar potency to MXE without the 3-MeO group.

notes: Eticyclidone. No published binding data; speculated NMDA Ki 100-400 nM based on structural homology.

name: Eticyclidone

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: See O-PCE.

notes: Same compound as O-PCE.

name: BTCP

binding.notes: Vignon 1988; IC50 7-8 nM for DA uptake. ~50× selectivity over SERT/NET.
Essentially inactive at NMDA — BTCP is a 'PCP without NMDA activity'

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Pure DAT inhibitor with cocaine-like behavioral profile (Le Foll 2000 Neuropsychopharmacology) but binds at a DAT site allosterically distinct from cocaine.

metabolism.notes: Two active hydroxylated metabolites bind DAT with Ki within 2× of parent

notes: Atypical arylcyclohexylamine — replacing the phenyl with benzothiophene shifts pharmacology entirely from NMDA blockade to DAT inhibition. Behaviorally cocaine-like, not PCP-like. Tag 'NMDA-antagonist' is wrong.

name: 3-pip-OH-BTCP

binding.notes: Hydroxylated BTCP metabolite; retains DAT affinity within 2× of parent

notes: Hydroxylated BTCP metabolite. Like parent, DAT-selective; not an NMDA blocker.

name: Tiletamine

binding.notes: No published Ki value identified in literature search.

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Thiophene-2 in place of phenyl ring. Functional in vivo profile similar to ketamine — used as Telazol (with zolazepam) in veterinary anesthesia.

metabolism.notes: Kumar 2014: marked species differences in metabolism. Pig liver microsomes show different pathways than human.

demographic_differences.renal_or_hepatic: Plasma t½ varies by species: cat 2.4 h, dog 1.2 h, monkey 1-1.5 h (pmid:17083465)

notes: Veterinary dissociative; component of Telazol (with zolazepam, 1:1). No published human PK or human Ki binding studies.

name: Tilmetamine

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: N-methyl analogue of tiletamine (vs N-ethyl). No published pharmacology.

notes: Research-chemical N-methyl variant of tiletamine. No published binding or PK data.

name: Rolicyclidine

binding.notes: PCPy is the pyrrolidine analogue of PCP; binds the PCP site. Roth 2013 did not include rolicyclidine. No quantitative Ki published; estimated similar potency to PCP based on classical SAR papers from 1970s (Maddox 1965).

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Slightly less potent than PCP per behavioral studies; less stimulant character.

notes: Synthesized in 1958 (Maddox/Parke-Davis). Never developed clinically. Schedule I in US.

name: 3-MeO-PCE

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: See 3-MeO-PCE record (with lowercase 'e' in input list duplicate).

notes: Cross-reference: see the original 3-MeO-PCE record (Ki 61 nM NMDA, Roth 2013). Same compound, distinct input list entry.

name: 3-Fluoro-PCP

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Meta-fluoro analogue of PCP. No published Ki. By SAR analogy to 3-MeO-PCP (very high NMDA affinity 20 nM) and 3-F bioisostere logic — expected NMDA Ki 30-100 nM range.

notes: Two entries in input list (3-F-PCP and 3-Fluoro-PCP refer to the same compound). No published binding data; estimated potency similar to or greater than PCP.

name: 3-F-PCP

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: See 3-Fluoro-PCP.

notes: Same compound as 3-Fluoro-PCP.

name: 3-EtO-PCP

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Ethoxy analogue of 3-MeO-PCP. Expected slight reduction in NMDA affinity vs methoxy (bulkier group in the 3-position). No published Ki.

notes: Emerging 2020s research chemical. Cases of intoxication documented but no published binding data.

name: 3-Me-PCPy
notes: Pyrrolidine + 3-methyl analogue. No published binding data.

name: 3-MeO-PCMo

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Morpholine analogue. The PCMo series (Wallach 2017 ACS Chem Neurosci doi:10.1021/acschemneuro.7b00269) showed 3-MeO morpholine analogues retain NMDA affinity but lower than the piperidine counterpart.

notes: Morpholine N-replacement of 3-MeO-PCP. Wallach group has reported the PCMo series shows ~10× lower NMDA affinity than the piperidine series.

name: 3-MeO-PCPr

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: N-propyl analogue of 3-MeO-PCE. Higher lipophilicity may extend duration.

notes: No published binding data.

name: 3-MeO-PCPy

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Pyrrolidine + 3-MeO analogue. No published Ki.

notes: No published binding data.

name: 3-ho-pce

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: By structural analogy to 3-HO-PCP, expected to combine NMDA antagonism + μ-opioid agonism. 3-HO-PCP MOR Ki 39-60 nM, KOR Ki 140 nM (Itzhak 1985). The 3-OH PCE analogue likely shares this profile but no formal data.

tolerance_and_dependence.withdrawal_syndrome: Possible opioid-like withdrawal in addition to NMDA-class withdrawal

notes: 3-HO-PCE is the N-ethyl analogue of 3-HO-PCP. Critical safety concern: 3-OH substitution at meta of arylcyclohexylamines confers μ-opioid agonism — major overdose risk (respiratory depression) when combined with NMDA blockade dissociation.

name: 2-Bromodeschloroketamine

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Br-for-Cl bioisostere of ketamine. Expected slightly higher NMDA affinity than ketamine (larger halogen, more lipophilic) but no formal binding data published.

notes: Same as Bromoketamine record.

name: Bromoketamine

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: See 2-Bromodeschloroketamine.

notes: Same compound as 2-Bromodeschloroketamine.

name: 2-Chlorodeschloroketamine

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: By definition this name is identical to ketamine itself (ketamine = 2-chlorophenyl). The name 'deschloroketamine' refers to removal of chloro, so '2-chlorodeschloroketamine' is contradictory; likely a market naming artifact for ketamine.

notes: Name is a contradiction. May refer to ketamine or to a different positional isomer per black-market vendor naming.

name: 2-FXE

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Fluoro-substituted analogue of FXE (3-F-2-oxo-PCE). No published binding data.

notes: Possibly equivalent to Canket / Fluorexetamine — name overlaps with these in marketplace usage.

name: 2-MeO-Ketamine

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Ortho-methoxy analogue of ketamine. Methoxy in 2-position replacing chloro. No published Ki; expected NMDA affinity similar to or slightly lower than ketamine because the ortho-methoxy may sterically interfere with PCP-site binding.

notes: Same as Methoxyketamine record.

name: Methoxyketamine

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: See 2-MeO-Ketamine.

notes: Same compound as 2-MeO-Ketamine.

name: 3,4-Methylenedioxy-phencyclidine

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Methylenedioxy in 3,4-position. No published binding data. Methylenedioxy substitution often introduces 5-HT2/SERT activity in other drug classes (MDMA vs methamphetamine) — possible additional serotonergic component vs PCP.

notes: No published binding data.

name: Allylketamine

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: N-allyl analogue of ketamine. Allyl groups often produce CYP-suicide-inhibition; PK consequences possible.

notes: N-substitution variant of ketamine. Abelian 2024 β-keto SAR paper (cited in task brief) covers N-alkyl variants but specific value not captured here.

name: Cyclobutylketamine

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: N-cyclobutyl analogue of ketamine. No published binding data.

notes: No published data.

name: Cyclopropylketamine

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: N-cyclopropyl analogue of ketamine. Cyclopropyl is a common 'metabolic stability' substitution.

notes: No published data.

name: Dimethylketamine

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: N,N-dimethyl analogue of ketamine. N,N-dialkyl substitution generally reduces NMDA affinity in the arylcyclohexylamine series — expected lower potency than parent ketamine.

notes: No published data.

name: DMXM
notes: Likely deoxy analogue of methoxmetamine. No published data.

name: Ethketamine

functional.notes: Han 2019: NENK, 2-MeO-NEK, 4-MeO-NEK produce rapid antidepressant-like effects via AMPA + 5-HT2 receptor activation. NENK = ethketamine.

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Han 2019: N-ethyl-norketamine series acts via AMPA + 5-HT2 pathway, similar to (2R,6R)-HNK proposed mechanism, but with retained NMDA activity.

class_name: Arylcyclohexylamines (NMDA antagonists at the PCP binding site)
shared_mechanism: Arylcyclohexylamines are use-dependent, voltage-sensitive, non-competitive blockers of the NMDA receptor channel at the PCP binding site within the central vestibule. Channel block requires the channel to be open (agonist-bound, depolarized). Cryo-EM structures of S-ketamine bound to GluN1/GluN2A and GluN1/GluN2B (Zhang 2021, doi:10.1038/s41586-021-03769-9) revealed two distinct sub-poses within the binding pocket, mediated primarily by hydrophobic and hydrogen-bond interactions with GluN2A-L642 (≡ GluN2B-L643) and GluN1-N616. The two-pose model rationalizes apparent SAR discrepancies. Beyond NMDA blockade, members of the class engage σ1 receptors (PCP, 3-MeO-PCP strongly; ketamine weakly), serotonin and other monoamine transporters (MXE family especially SERT; 3-MeO-PCP SERT; PCP weakly DAT), HCN1 channels (ketamine, anesthetic relevance), and μ/κ-opioid receptors (3-HO-PCP strongly; ketamine weakly — debated as functional contributor to antidepressant action). The major ketamine metabolite (2R,6R)-hydroxynorketamine does NOT block NMDA at antidepressant-relevant concentrations and instead acts via α7-nAChR-dependent presynaptic glutamate release plus AMPA potentiation (Marcantoni 2024, Suzuki 2017).
shared_pk_summary: Hepatic CYP-mediated metabolism dominates the class. Ketamine cleared predominantly by CYP2B6 and CYP3A4 to norketamine (active, 3× less potent at NMDA), then to (2R,6R)-HNK and dehydronorketamine. Oral routes give norketamine >> parent drug due to first-pass (norketamine/ketamine plasma ratio ~6:1). Bioavailability: IV 100%, IM ~93%, intranasal 25-50%, sublingual ~25-30%, oral ~17-25%. Half-lives 2-4 h for ketamine class; PCP is an outlier at 1-3 days due to high lipophilicity. Protein binding 12-50% across the class. CYP2B6*6/*6 PMs show ~50% reduction in oral ketamine clearance with implications for TRD therapy.
shared_safety: Acute risk: respiratory depression at high doses (potentiated when combined with opioids or alcohol). Cardiovascular sympathomimetic effects (HR/BP increase). Emergence delirium, dissociation, occasional violent psychomotor agitation (highest for 3-MeO-PCP, 3-MeO-PCE, PCP). Hepatic toxicity — case reports for some research chemicals. Chronic risk: ulcerative cystitis (norketamine implicated) in heavy daily users; cognitive impairment; psychological dependence. Key off-targets: HCN1 (ketamine hypnosis), σ1 (3-MeO-PCP psychosis profile), μ-opioid (3-HO-PCP/E respiratory depression). Fatal blood concentrations: PCP >200 ng/mL, 3-MeO-PCP 50-3,525 ng/mL (very narrow window), ketamine >1,000 ng/mL (very wide therapeutic index).
sar_summary: Core scaffold: phenyl + cyclohexyl + amine. SAR principles, with primary literature: (1) Aryl ring substitution dominates NMDA affinity: 3-methoxy > 3-ethoxy > 3-methyl > 3-fluoro > H > 2-chloro (ketamine); 4-position less effective than 3-position (Roth 2013 doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0059334). (2) 2'-oxo (β-keto) substitution: shortens duration, restricts conformation, shifts pose preference at PCP site (Zhang 2021), produces 'heavier' subjective profile per Abelian 2024 SAR analysis. (3) N-amine: N-methyl (ketamine) > N-ethyl (MXE/O-PCE) > N-propyl > N-cyclopropyl; primary amine (norketamine) ~3× less potent than N-methyl. Piperidine (PCP) and pyrrolidine (rolicyclidine) typically more potent at NMDA than secondary amines but with different σ1 and PK profiles. (4) Combining 2'-oxo + 3-MeO + piperidine (MXPCP-like) predicted maximum NMDA affinity. (5) Aryl ring replacement: thiophene-2 (tiletamine) retains NMDA activity; benzothiophene-2 (BTCP) eliminates NMDA and switches to DAT-selective. (6) Meta-OH (3-HO-PCP/E series) introduces μ-opioid agonism alongside NMDA blockade — major safety implication.
